name: Everything typed after
hint: everything typed after the command
description: All text after the command, as one string.

name: Channel name
hint: the channel the command runs in
description: Your channel's display name.

name: Command name
hint: the command’s own name, without the “!”
description: The name of the command that ran, without the "!". Alternate names all report the main one.

name: Named person
hint: first argument, e.g. a mentioned user
description: The first word typed after the command ("@" removed); the viewer themself when blank. {target} works too.

name: Viewer name
hint: who ran the command
description: Whoever used the command. {sender} works too.

name: Viewer ID
hint: the Twitch user ID of whoever ran the command
description: The viewer's Twitch user ID. It never changes, even after a rename.

name: Viewer login
hint: their lowercase login, not their display name
description: Their lowercase login, which can differ from the display name {user} shows.

name: Word number
hint: word 1 typed after the command; {2} is the next one, up to {30}; {2:4} takes a range
description: Word 1 typed after the command. {2} is the next one, and so on up to {30}. Empty when that word was not typed. {2:} takes a word through to the end, as one string; change the number to start elsewhere, {1:} is the whole thing. {2:4} takes words 2 through 4 the same way, and {:2} is the same range starting at word 1 (the first two words). Naming an end past the last word actually typed just stops at that last word; naming the end before the start, like {4:2}, is left exactly as written.

name: Counter
hint: shows a counter's current value; {count:…} is the same read (Loyalty)
description: Shows a counter's current value without changing it. To add to a counter, turn on "Bump a counter" on the command itself; this only reads whatever that option (or !counter) has produced. {counter:target:name} reads the mentioned viewer's own count instead of the channel's. Needs the Loyalty Points module.

name: Times used
hint: how many times this command has been used, not counting this one; {uses} is the same thing (approximate)
description: How many times this command has been used in your channel, not counting the one printing it. It counts every use, whichever name was typed, and needs no counter. {uses} is the older spelling of the same value. The total is approximate: the bot batches its counting, so it can be up to a minute behind.

name: Random choice
hint: picks one of the comma-separated options at random
description: Picks one of your comma-separated options. Replace the words.

name: Random 1-100
hint: a random number from 1 to 100, or {random:min-max}
description: A whole number from 1 to 100, new every time. {random:1-6} picks your own range; both ends included.

name: Time until a date
hint: how long until that date (YYYY-MM-DD, or a full timestamp)
description: How long until that date. Write it as YYYY-MM-DD, or as a full timestamp. Nothing once the date has passed.

name: Time since a date
hint: how long since that date
description: How long since that date, in the same wording as !uptime.

name: Say one thing or another
hint: one text or another: {if:name:when it has something:when it does not}, or {if:name=value:…:…} for an exact match. Variables do not work inside the two texts
description: Picks the first text when the variable you name has something in it, the second when it does not. Name it without braces, and write {if:game=Chess:…:…} to test an exact value instead. Variables do not work inside the two texts. Leave the second one out and a false test says nothing at all, if that empties the whole line, the bot skips that line rather than sending a blank message.

name: Arithmetic
hint: evaluates a small sum: + - * / and parentheses
description: Works out a small sum. Whole numbers, + - * / and parentheses; nothing else.

name: URL-encode a path
hint: URL-encodes the text for a path, not a query
description: The same, for the path part of a URL, where a space is not a plus.

name: URL-encode text
hint: URL-encodes the text you put after the colon
description: Encodes your own text for the query part of a URL. Replace the words.

name: Arguments, URL-encoded
hint: everything typed after the command, URL-encoded for a data source
description: Everything typed after the command, encoded so it can be dropped into a data source URL.

Quote #12: bagels are just savoury donuts (2026-01-31)

name: A saved quote
hint: a random saved quote, or {quote:12} for a numbered one (Quotes module)
description: A random quote from your quote book, worded exactly as !quote says it. {quote:12} picks a numbered one, and a number nobody has used comes back empty. Two {quote} in one response are two different quotes. Needs the Quotes module.

name: Repeat a phrase
hint: repeats a phrase n times (up to 20, one chat line)
description: Repeats your phrase, space separated. Up to 20 times, and it has to fit one chat line.

name: Your local time
hint: your local time, on the clock face you set (Local time module); {time:Paris} for anywhere else, no module needed
description: The time where you are, on the timezone and clock face you set on the Local time module. Needs that module, with a timezone saved. {time:Paris} looks up a different place instead — a city, a country, an abbreviation like EST or a UTC offset — and works even without the module: it just needs no timezone of its own, only the clock face you picked if you ever set one. A place it does not recognize comes back empty.

name: Fetched value
hint: Insert a fetched value from a saved API definition
description: One value from a saved data source definition (Data sources page). Write {urlfetch:name} for the whole response, or add a dot path to reach one field inside a JSON response, such as {urlfetch:weather.forecast.current.temp_f}.

name: Account age
hint: how old their Twitch account is (Account age module)
description: How old their Twitch account is. {accountage:alex} asks about someone else. Needs the Account age module.

name: Time following
hint: how long they have followed the channel (Followage module)
description: How long the viewer has followed you, in the same wording as !followage. {followage:alex} asks about someone else, and someone who does not follow comes back empty. Needs the Followage module.

name: Points balance
hint: their points balance, or {points:login} for someone else (Loyalty)
description: What the viewer has earned. {points:alex} shows someone else, as long as this channel has seen them speak. Reading only: it never grants. Needs the Loyalty Points module.

name: Name of your points
hint: your channel’s name for its points (Loyalty)
description: Whatever you called your points in the Loyalty Points module, so one reply reads right on every channel.

name: Time watched
hint: how long they have watched, in the same words as !uptime (Loyalty)
description: How long they have watched while the loyalty clock was running. {watchtime:alex} asks about someone else. Needs the Loyalty Points module.

name: Viewers watching
hint: how many people are watching right now, 0 when you are offline
description: How many people are watching right now, straight from Twitch. An offline channel comes back as 0. Bare {channel} stays your channel name.

name: Follower count
hint: your current follower count
description: Your current follower count, straight from Twitch. Takes no payload — it always counts your own channel.

name: Stream category
hint: the category you are streaming, or {game:someone} for another channel (!game toggle)
description: The category being streamed, the same one !game shows. It works offline too. {game:someone} gives another channel’s, which is what a shoutout command wants. Follows the !game toggle.

name: Subscriber count
hint: your current subscriber count
description: Your current subscriber count, straight from Twitch. Takes no payload — it always counts your own channel.

name: Stream title
hint: your current stream title, or {title:someone} for another channel (!title toggle)
description: The current stream title, the same one !title shows. It works offline too. {title:someone} gives another channel’s. Follows the !title toggle.

name: Stream uptime
hint: how long you have been live, empty when you are offline (!uptime toggle)
description: How long the stream has been live, worded the way !uptime words it. Offline comes back empty, so give it a default. {uptime:someone} does the same for another channel. Follows the !uptime toggle.

name: People in chat
hint: how many people have talked in chat recently
description: How many people have talked in chat recently. It counts chatters the bot has seen speak, not everyone with the page open, and a quiet channel comes back as 0.

name: Clip link
description: The freshly created clip link.

name: Local date
description: Today's date in your timezone.

name: Raider name
description: Friendly display name of the raiding channel.

name: Raider login
description: URL-safe login, for twitch.tv/ links.

name: A random chatter
hint: one of them, picked at random (never you, never the bot)
description: The name of one person who has talked recently, picked at random. Never you and never the bot. Two of them in one response are two separate picks, and a silent channel comes back empty.

name: A random viewer
hint: someone in chat right now, picked at random (never you, never the bot)
description: The name of one person Twitch says is in chat right now, picked at random — not someone who has necessarily said anything. Never you and never the bot. Two of them in one response are two separate picks. Right after the bot restarts, before it has loaded who is in chat, it names someone who has spoken recently instead.

name: Clip title
description: The title typed after !clip.

name: Timezone
description: The configured timezone name.

name: Emote list
hint: every global emote code from one provider — {emotes:7tv}, {emotes:bttv} or {emotes:ffz} — space-separated
description: The global emote codes for one provider (7TV, BetterTTV or FrankerFaceZ), separated by spaces. These are the ones every channel has, not the emotes you added to yours, and a long list is cut to fit one chat line.

name: A random emote
hint: one emote code picked at random from those global sets
description: One emote code drawn at random from those lists. Two of them in one response are two separate picks. If the bot has not loaded any codes yet, it comes back empty.

name: Bits amount
description: How many bits were cheered.

name: Sub tier
description: The subscription tier.

name: Raid size
description: How many viewers arrived.

name: Point cost
description: What the reward costs.

name: Viewer input
description: The text typed with the redemption (when the reward asks for one).

name: Reward title
description: The name of the redeemed reward.

name: Queue position
description: Their spot in line.

hint: the track playing right now, or {song.title} / {song.artist} (Song requests)

name: Song artist
hint: just the artist name, the second half of {song}
description: The artist name on its own, the second half of {song}. Nothing playing comes back empty. Needs the Song requests module.

name: Song title
hint: just the track title, the first half of {song}
description: The track title on its own, the first half of {song}. Nothing playing comes back empty. Needs the Song requests module.
